title: Probe-driven occlusion detector and contextual release synthesizer
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: some model rollouts cause subtle, cohort-specific regressions that are not obvious from global metrics. This PR introduces a probe-driven 'occlusion detector' that compares live-sampled probe telemetry against a baseline cohort fingerprint and synthesizes a compact, contextual release digest that highlights affected prompt cohorts and suggested remediation actions (score, rollback hint, minimal repro).

What this PR does (high level): 1) Adds a sampled telemetry union pipeline to merge periodic probe samples with production request traces while preserving privacy/sampling guarantees. 2) Implements an occlusion detector that computes per-cohort delta statistics (accuracy/semantic-distance/latency) and flags cohorts exceeding configurable thresholds. 3) Generates a contextual release synth — a human-readable changelog fragment that summarizes which cohorts regressed, sample prompts, expected impact, and an automated 'rollback score' suggestion based on severity and traffic weight. 4) Integrates the digest as an optional attachment to release notes and as a webhook payload for incident tooling.

Why unique: instead of only surfacing numeric deltas, the detector collates representative prompts and links to the model-profile + perf-profile diffs so release authors and SREs can quickly assess risk and triage. It targets the recurring class of regressions that show up in low-volume but business-critical cohorts.

Compatibility and safety: the telemetry union runs as a rate-limited background exporter and strips PII from prompts using existing scrubbers. Default thresholds are conservative and require at least two consecutive probe windows before a cohort is auto-flagged.

Related work: ENG-1245 (cohort telemetry sampling), PR:redwood-model-registry#17345 (baseline samplers), and the rollout playbook for canaries.

Checklist: - [x] Telemetry union pipeline (sampling operator + scrubber) - [x] Occlusion detector core logic and threshold config - [x] Compact release synth generation and template - [x] Webhook + release note attachment support - [x] Unit + integration tests for detector heuristics - [x] Docs: short guide for release authors

review_conversation:
Marcus Lee: Please clarify how the scrubber handles edge cases like code snippets that might look like PII.
Sofia Patel: We added a two-step rule — first apply token-level heuristic redaction then a regex pass for common PII forms. Added tests for code-like payloads to ensure we don't over-redact.
Priya Nair: Can the detector be noisy for very small cohorts?
Sofia Patel: Defaults require a minimum sample count and two consecutive probe windows before auto-flagging; added a tunable 'minimum_traffic_weight' parameter.
Evan Chen: How do we surface this to non-technical release authors?
Sofia Patel: The synth produces a short bullet summary and an optional expanded appendix with representative prompts and links to profile diffs; docs include examples.
Marcus Lee: CI flake on Linux integration fixed in fa8b4d2; approving.
Evan Chen: Approved after minor docs tweaks.
release_notes:
- Add probe-driven occlusion detector: flags cohort-specific regressions and synthesizes contextual release digests.
- Telemetry union pipeline for sampled probe + production trace merging (PII-scrubbed).
- Webhook and release attachment support to include contextual digests with release notes.
notes_for_release_authors: When enabling the occlusion detector, start with the 'conservative' preset. The digest includes a rollback_score (0-100) and suggested next steps; treat >70 as high risk for immediate rollback. The detector respects existing canary/fallback policies. See docs/model-registry/release-occlusion-guide.md for examples.
